text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zambian press on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The government has withdrawn a controversial media reform bill, pending further consultations.
- Border officials at Zaire's Kasumbalesa border post have abandoned their positions, allowing people and traffic to enter Zambia freely.
- Over 1,000 workers on the Tanzania-Zambia Railway Authority (Tazara) have gone for two months without pay.

- Mines minister Christon Tembo says Zambia Consolidated Copper Mines (ZCCM) workers will be allowed to purchase the company-owned houses they live in ahead of the privatisation of the mining conglomerate.
- An election official, testifying in a legal challenge to the outcome of presidential and parliamentary elections held last year, said some people voted more than once.
- The government says local government elections have been delayed indefinitely because of a lack of resources.
- Zambia Consolidated Copper Mines (ZCCM) recorded lower copper output in February.
